learning_outcomes.text: Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering that aim at the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing and automation processes.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to organize and plan within the company, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge and abilities to organize and manage projects. Knowing the organizational structure and functions of a project office.

syllabus_topics: Regulations and certification in building: Technical Building Code. Determination of actions. Sizing of sections. Sizing of bars.
Regulations and certification in pressure vessels: ASME VIII Code. Determination of thicknesses in pressure vessels. Determination of thicknesses in welded joints. Calculation of heads.
Economic aspects in building. Calculation of unit prices and budget items. Calculation of the final budget. Project profitability: NPV and IRR. Main economic parameters.
Project Management. GANTT, PERT, CPM, ROY methods.
assessment_rules: The general assessment model is continuous assessment. No individual assessment activity may exceed 60% of the global grade, and non-re-evaluable activities cannot exceed 40%. A minimum score of 4.0 is required for each formative test, with an average of 5.0 or higher, and a minimum of 5.0 for the project presentation and design project. Students must present and orally defend the Project Report, and those who do not pass or attend the ordinary call can only retake re-evaluable activities in the extraordinary call.
